categories.description: Managed APIs and platforms for building AI-powered applications with hosted state, tools, files, retrieval, execution, memory, identity, and governance.
No/low-code canvases and automation platforms for composing AI application workflows, agents, and tool integrations.
Code-first frameworks and runtimes for building tool-using, stateful AI applications with routing, memory, planning, orchestration, handoffs, and human-in-the-loop flows.
Protocols, action layers, and connector systems that expose data, tools, prompts, and business actions to AI applications.
Evaluation, tracing, debugging, A/B testing, prompt/version management, analytics, and production monitoring for AI applications.
Safety, validation, policy enforcement, prompt-injection defense, moderation, and output constraints for AI applications.

options.name: PydanticAI
options.notes: Type-safe agent framework with structured outputs, tools, MCP, durable execution, and realtime model support. v2.52.0 (September 30) adds workspaces so harness tools (Coder, Shell, FileSystem) run locally or in E2B, Modal, or Fly.io Sprite sandboxes, and folds pydantic-ai-harness into every release; v2.55.0 (October 9) adds a `Conversation` object carried between runs, cross-provider prompt caching, and Postgres message/media stores, and requires Python 3.11+.

options.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
options.notes: Framework for agents, handoffs, sessions, tracing, guardrails, and sandboxed execution. v0.23.0 (October 1) adds configurable MCP listing page limits, opt-in Docker sandbox removal protection, configurable memory-consolidation turns, and an encrypted session-history scan budget, plus redaction of tool failure details and stricter tool-approval scoping.

options.name: Claude Agent SDK
options.notes: Agent SDK built on Claude Code, with sessions, file and shell tools, permissions, hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, and MCP. Python v0.2.153 (September 15) adds system-prompt snapshots and v0.2.158 (September 23) a `verbatim_prompts` option; v0.2.165 (October 8) bundles Claude CLI 2.1.294.

options.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
options.notes: Successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel for provider-neutral agents, workflows, checkpoints, approvals, and Foundry integration. Python 1.18-1.19 (September 10-18) add shared vector-store abstractions with Azure AI Search, Redis, Cosmos DB, Qdrant, Postgres, and MongoDB connectors; 1.20.0 (October 2) redesigns Foundry hosting around persistent sandbox-isolated sessions and adds native computer use, and 1.21.0 (October 8) adds a maximum reasoning-effort option and an Oracle vector store.

options.name: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
options.notes: Open-source framework for agents, tools, workflows, evaluation, and Google Cloud deployment, with Python, TypeScript, Go, and Java libraries. Python 2.9.0 (September 10) adds automatic model failover, a LiveKit voice runner, YAML-defined graph workflows, and MCP SDK 2.x; 2.10.0 (September 24) adds skill lifecycles and efficiency eval metrics, and 2.11.0 (October 1) adds run cancellation, tool confirmation in workflows, a ModelConsultTool, and a SQLite memory service.

options.name: Responses API
options.notes: OpenAI's primary agent API, with persistent conversations, built-in tools, remote MCP, and programmatic tool calling. Prompt Cache Diagnostics became generally available September 8; GPT-6.1 Sol (September 29) brings Multi-agent in beta through the Responses API, and an Ultrafast service tier (service_tier: "ultrafast") followed for GPT-6 Astra and, on October 8, GPT-6.1 Sol.

options.name: OpenAI Assistants API
options.notes: Retired on August 26, 2026. Hosted assistant, thread, and run integrations must migrate to the Responses API and Conversations API.

options.name: Anthropic Messages (Tool Use & Computer Use)
options.notes: Claude's API for text, image, and structured tool use, with computer and browser toolsets. September added on-demand compaction (beta, September 14), cache diagnostics GA (September 23), and tools defined in mid-conversation system messages without breaking the prompt cache (beta, September 22) alongside Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 launches; October 7 SDK releases add beta helper classes that run the computer-use and browser-use tool loop.

options.name: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
options.notes: Google Cloud's managed agent platform, including config-driven Managed Agents, Agent Engine, enterprise search and grounding, tools, A2A interoperability, sandboxed execution, and persistent state. Computer Use and Shell sandboxes became generally available September 9 with VPC Service Controls, CMEK, and pause/resume, and Agent Platform SDK for Python 2.0.1 (September 18) moves the agent surface into a separate google-cloud-agentplatform package.

options.name: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
options.notes: Managed platform for prompt agents and hosted code agents, with Responses-compatible endpoints, model choice, tools, identity, scaling, observability, private networking, evaluations, and A2A support.

options.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
options.notes: Managed runtime and services for agents, including harness, browser, code interpreter, memory, identity, gateway, observability, evaluations, policies, and AWS Agent Registry. September 2026 added harness lifecycle hooks (Lambda allow/deny plus SNS/EventBridge notifications), persistent interactive shells over WebSocket, an Identity Consent Portal, and TypeScript framework support in Evaluations; October brought Gateway support for targets with private-CA TLS certificates.

options.name: OpenRouter Actions
options.notes: Model routing + tool/action execution as a hosted layer for agents.

options.name: LangChain
options.notes: Agent framework for tool calling, model integrations, middleware, and memory, built on LangGraph for durable, stateful agents. langchain 1.4.3 (September 28) adds Bedrock Mantle models to `init_chat_model` and repairs invalid tool calls in `create_agent`; 1.4.4 (October 8) retries summarization on context overflow.

options.name: LangGraph
options.notes: Graph-based runtime for stateful agents with durable execution, interrupts, resumable workflows, and human review. 1.2.12 (September 21) adds a `response_schema` to `interrupt()`, the CLI 0.4.32 (September 23) adds self-hosted deployment options, and 1.2.13 (October 5) fixes checkpoint forking and replay.

options.name: LlamaIndex
options.notes: RAG-first agents, tools, routers, observability; integrates with many vector stores.

options.name: Semantic Kernel
options.notes: Established Microsoft SDK for plugins, connectors, memory, and agent orchestration. Microsoft Agent Framework is its direct next-generation successor; migration guidance is available for active projects.

options.name: DSPy
options.notes: Declarative LLM programming framework that optimizes prompts and weights for chains and agents. DSPy 3.4.0 (September 25) adds Jev integration through the TypeSafe client, with experimental `Noul`, `Choice`, and `Score` decision types that return probabilities and confidence, and starts the LM-type migration due by 3.5.

options.name: Haystack Agents
options.notes: Pipelines and agents with strong RAG and tool integration. Haystack 3.2.0 (September 24) adds an experimental SummarizationCompactor for agent context compaction and a TokenBudgetHook that caps tokens per agent run; 3.3.0 (October 1) speeds up SentenceWindowRetriever and fixes CJK BM25 tokenization.

options.name: Temporal.io
options.notes: Durable workflow orchestration used for long-running agent processes, providing retries, state persistence, and production reliability; often paired with OpenAI Agents SDK or LangGraph. Server v1.32.0 (September 11) makes Standalone Activities generally available and previews Standalone Nexus Operations started directly from a client.

options.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
options.notes: Open interoperability standard (2024) for exposing tools, data, and prompts to AI applications; adopted across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and most agent frameworks. The 2026-07-28 specification (published July 28, 2026) makes the protocol core stateless (no session handshake), adds Multi Round-Trip Requests, header-based routing, cacheable list results, hardened authorization (DCR deprecated in favor of CIMD), and a formal extensions framework (Tasks, MCP Apps, Enterprise Managed Authorization); Roots, Sampling, and Logging are deprecated. Tier 1 SDKs: TypeScript, Python, Go, C# (Rust in beta).

options.name: Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
options.notes: Open agent-to-agent interoperability protocol for discovery through Agent Cards, task delegation, streaming, and long-running collaboration across frameworks and vendors. Complements MCP's tool and context integration role.

options.name: Agent User Interaction Protocol (AG-UI)
options.notes: Event-based protocol connecting agent backends to interactive frontends, covering streaming messages, tool calls, shared state, generative UI, and human-in-the-loop interaction. AG-UI 1.0 (September 17) freezes the specification and JSON Schema, with generated 1.0 SDKs for TypeScript, Python, and .NET and protobuf wire support.

options.name: AutoGen
options.notes: Established conversational multi-agent framework with tool, model, human, and group-chat patterns. Microsoft Agent Framework is its direct next-generation successor; migration guidance is available for active projects.

options.name: crewAI
options.notes: Role-based multi-agent teams, tasks, tools, flows, skills, and process supervision. 1.15.22-1.15.27 releases (September 16-October 9) add an `llm_overlay` to route agent roles to models, native Gemini 3.8 Flash, `crewai eval` with multi-model comparison and per-run cost tracking, Oracle integrations, an experimental job lifecycle runner, and DeepInfra as a provider.

options.name: FlowiseAI
options.notes: Open-source drag-and-drop builder for LLM agents and chatflows. The maintainers wound the project down: active development stopped July 29, 2026, and the GitHub repository was archived read-only on August 13, 2026, with npm packages and Docker images deprecated; the Apache 2.0 code remains available for forks.

options.name: n8n (AI + Agents)
options.notes: Workflow automation platform with LLM nodes, tools, and webhooks to operationalize agents. n8n Agents (preview on Cloud, beta self-hosted, from v2.32.3; announced August 5, 2026) are define-once agents with their own tab, usable from chat, workflows, Slack/Telegram/Linear channels, or schedules, with MCP tools, skills, sub-agents, memory, versioning, and approvals.

options.name: Zapier AI Actions
options.notes: Natural-language actions that let agents operate 6000+ SaaS apps securely.

options.name: Langfuse
options.notes: Agent tracing, prompt management, datasets, and evaluation platform; v4 became generally available August 17. September added evaluator backfills over up to six months of past observations (September 7), sandboxed bulk analysis by the Langfuse Assistant, rebuilt experiment results, and a Jev-as-a-judge evaluator option; Langfuse Cloud becomes v4-only on November 16.

options.name: Weights & Biases (Weave/Evals)
options.notes: Experiment tracking plus eval pipelines and dashboards for agent performance.

options.name: OpenAI Evals
options.notes: Regression tests and dataset-driven evals to guard agent quality over time.

options.name: AgentScope
options.notes: Developer-centric agent framework with unified interfaces, async execution, sandboxing, and eval tooling. v2.0.8 (September 8) adds a realtime voice agent, an A2AAgent, and agent-driven context compression; v2.0.9 (September 28) adds experimental standard operating procedures, a TeamPipeline, OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live, and Grok Voice models, and a terminal UI.

options.name: Agent Lightning
options.notes: Microsoft's RL training framework for agents, decoupled from agent execution, with integrations for LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, and AutoGen. v1.0.2 (September 29) adds MoE coding-agent training for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with CISPO and expert-routing replay, and passes image inputs from rollout traces into training.

options.name: Cerebrum (AIOS SDK)
options.notes: Provides agent SDK, hub, and testing/eval features. Supports deployment, discovery, and distribution.

options.name: Guardrails AI
options.notes: Schema validation, semantic checks, moderation & policy enforcement for agents.

options.name: NeMo Guardrails
options.notes: Rail-spec safety & grounded flows; complements NVIDIA NIM and RAG stacks.

options.name: Rebuff
options.notes: Prompt-injection detection library combining heuristics, an LLM detector, a vector store of past attacks, and canary tokens. The GitHub repository is archived (read-only) and has had no code changes since August 2024.

options.name: Agent Plugins
options.provider: Agent Plugins core maintainers (AWS, Cursor, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Vercel)
options.notes: Vendor-neutral open standard (1.0.0, Aug 6, 2026) that packages Agent Skills and MCP servers into a single installable plugin folder (plugin.json, skills/, mcp.json). Launch clients include ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Kiro, and VS Code; the plugins CLI can also target Claude Code. Governance charter prevents any single vendor from holding a majority of maintainer seats; permission model, sandboxing, and signing are future work.

options.name: Mastra
options.notes: TypeScript agent framework with agents, tools, workflows, memory, RAG, evals, observability, MCP, and AG-UI. Core 1.68 (September 23) ships `@mastra/mcp` 2.0 on the MCP 2026-07-28 revision and Azure AI Search and Weaviate vector stores; 1.70 (September 25) adds per-request model routing, and 1.75 (October 7) adds span queries with token/cost aggregation and a stable `@mastra/connect` 1.0 with Microsoft Teams channels.

options.name: Claude Managed Agents
options.notes: Managed Claude agent service with environments, skills, memory stores, and deployment controls. September 10 added an auto permission policy that lets the server run, deny, or pause each tool call for approval, plus ant CLI 1.32 to attach a terminal to a running session; October 9 added dynamic workflows (beta), where an agent writes a program that runs many agents in phases.

options.name: Mistral Search Toolkit
options.notes: Retrieval toolkit for ingesting, embedding, and indexing enterprise documents. Agentic Search (August 20) lets agents search, open, navigate, read, and inspect sources through a multi-step retrieval loop, also available in Libraries across Studio and Vibe.

options.name: Sarvam Voice Agents
options.notes: Platform for building, deploying, and monitoring voice agents on telephony. September added a hosted Voice Agents MCP server (September 16) and regression tests with simulated users graded by an AI judge (September 17); Bulbul V4 voices became selectable per agent on October 6.

options.name: Gemini Enterprise Workflow Builder
options.notes: Workflow Builder, formerly Agent Designer, became generally available September 3. Builds scheduled or on-demand workflows, connects enterprise applications, imports ADK and A2A agents, and makes workflows and chat agents available through chat mentions under administrator controls.

options.name: DeepSeek Harness
options.notes: Developer preview of DeepSeek's open-source agent runtime, built on Cordis with a plugin-based architecture; the dsh CLI starts a local web interface. v0.2.0-rc.1 (September 28) is the first 0.2.0 release candidate, moving automations into an optional plugin pack, and v0.2.1-alpha.2 (October 9) adds an experimental Git Worktrees plugin, shared AGENTS.md instructions, and working-directory APIs in the TypeScript and Python SDKs.

options.name: OpenAI Agents API
options.notes: OpenAI's managed agent API built on the Codex harness, with durable sessions, streaming, custom tools and MCP servers, and OpenAI-hosted or customer-provided sandboxes; public beta since September 10, 2026. Computer use in an OpenAI-hosted browser was added September 29.

description: Platforms, frameworks, protocols, evaluation tools, and guardrails for building applications that use AI agents. SDLC-support products such as coding agents, IDE assistants, and PR review agents live in software-engineering.json.
